question: What is the main goal of a medical abortion?

options.A: To prevent fertilization before intercourse occurs
options.B: To treat severe pelvic inflammatory disease infections
options.C: To dilate the cervix prior to surgical removal
options.D: To terminate an early pregnancy using drugs

explanation: Medication abortion relies on specific pharmaceutical agents rather than surgical instruments to end an early pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h1)

question: Why is medical abortion helpful in clinics with limited resources?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any patient follow-up
options.B: It requires fewer routine surgical theatre resources
options.C: It guarantees an immediate end to bleeding within an hour
options.D: It prevents all future sexually transmitted infections

explanation: By avoiding invasive procedures, medical termination reduces the demand on busy operating theatres and specialized surgical staff. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h1)

question: What is the main job of mifepristone during a medical abortion?

options.A: Stimulate strong muscular contractions of the myometrium
options.B: Block progesterone to break down the uterine lining
options.C: Prevent severe nausea and vomiting during the procedure
options.D: Induce rapid systemic vasoconstriction to limit blood loss

explanation: Mifepristone acts as an antiprogestin, preparing the uterus by breaking down its lining and softening the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: How does misoprostol help complete the process started by mifepristone?

options.A: It causes rhythmic uterine contractions to expel the tissue
options.B: It kills any remaining embryonic cells through direct toxicity
options.C: It permanently blocks estrogen receptors in ovarian tissue
options.D: It neutralizes remaining hormones to stop secondary bleeding

explanation: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin that stimulates the myometrium to contract and empty the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: Which condition means a patient should NOT receive a medical abortion?

options.A: History of primary dysmenorrhea and heavy periods
options.C: A gestational age of exactly four completed weeks
options.D: Mild iron deficiency anemia treated with supplements

explanation: Medical abortion drugs do not treat ectopic pregnancies and will leave the patient at high risk for dangerous tubal rupture. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h3)

question: A patient with an intrauterine device (IUD) in place asks for abortion pills. What must be done first?

options.A: The medication dose should be doubled to compensate for the device
options.B: The intrauterine device must be removed before starting pills
options.C: The client can take the pills immediately without any changes
options.D: She must be referred directly for a major abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: An existing IUD must be removed prior to a medication abortion to lower the risk of severe infection and treatment failure. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h3)

question: Why is it necessary to confirm a pregnancy is inside the uterus before giving abortion drugs?

options.A: To determine if the patient has a history of bleeding disorders
options.B: To accurately calculate the exact birth weight of the fetus
options.C: To ensure the drugs will not harm an undetected ectopic pregnancy
options.D: To verify the blood group and rhesus factor of the mother

explanation: Failing to rule out an ectopic pregnancy before giving abortifacient drugs can lead to catastrophic internal hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h4)

question: What is an important part of counseling a patient before a medical abortion?

options.A: Scheduling a mandatory surgical procedure for the following day
options.B: Instructing the client to fast for forty-eight hours prior
options.C: Explaining expected bleeding patterns and warning signs
options.D: Demanding a signed letter from a family member or partner

explanation: Patients need clear guidance on normal symptoms versus red flags so they can manage expectations and seek help promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h4)

question: How is mifepristone normally given in standard care?

options.A: Swallowed orally as a single pill
options.B: Inserted deeply into the vaginal vault
options.C: Applied topically onto the lower abdomen
options.D: Injected slowly into an intravenous line

explanation: Mifepristone is administered orally by the patient, usually under the direct observation of a healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h5)

question: How much time should usually pass between taking mifepristone and taking misoprostol?

options.A: Only when heavy bleeding starts spontaneously
options.B: Exactly ten minutes after swallowing the first drug
options.C: One full week after the initial clinic visit

explanation: Allowing up to forty-eight hours for mifepristone to sensitize the uterus ensures that subsequent misoprostol will work effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h5)

question: Which symptom is a normal part of a medical abortion?

options.A: Strong uterine cramping and heavy vaginal bleeding
options.B: Permanent cessation of all future menstrual cycles
options.C: Complete absence of any pain throughout the process
options.D: Sudden swelling and redness of the lower extremities

explanation: Cramping and bleeding are the expected physical mechanisms by which the uterine contents are successfully expelled. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h6)

question: A patient reports mild chills and low-grade fever two hours after using misoprostol. How should a nurse interpret this?

options.A: This indicates a severe, life-threatening septic uterine infection
options.B: The medication failed to work and she needs surgery immediately
options.C: She is experiencing a severe allergic reaction to mifepristone
options.D: These are common temporary side effects of the misoprostol

explanation: Misoprostol frequently causes temporary side effects like chills and low-grade fever that resolve on their own without treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h6)

question: Which finding shows excessive bleeding that needs immediate medical care?

options.A: Spotting light brown discharge for two weeks
options.B: Experiencing mild bleeding lighter than a normal period
options.C: Passing small blood clots the size of a coin
options.D: Soaking two large sanitary pads per hour for two hours

explanation: Soaking two pads an hour for two hours straight is the standard clinical threshold for heavy hemorrhage requiring intervention. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h7)

question: A patient returns four days after treatment with foul-smelling vaginal discharge and fever. What is the most likely issue?

options.A: An allergic rash caused by the oral mifepristone
options.B: Successful and complete emptying of the uterus
options.C: A normal physiological reaction to the misoprostol
options.D: Uterine infection or incomplete tissue expulsion

explanation: Foul discharge and persistent fever point toward retained products of conception leading to secondary uterine infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h7)

question: How soon can a patient get pregnant again after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting at least six months
options.B: Not until her natural menopause begins
options.C: As early as two weeks post-procedure
options.D: After a mandatory waiting period of one year

explanation: Ovulation can resume very quickly after an abortion, making prompt contraceptive initiation essential to prevent immediate repeat pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h8)

question: A patient wants an injectable contraceptive before leaving the clinic after her medical abortion. What is the correct nursing action?

options.A: Schedule a surgical procedure to insert an implant instead
options.B: Refuse the request and insist she wait for three months
options.C: Tell her contraceptives cannot be used after an abortion
options.D: Administer the injection immediately during the visit

explanation: Most modern contraceptive methods can be safely started on the same day as mifepristone or misoprostol administration. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h8)
